# PROCESS — cand_0006 (parent: cand_0001, champion val 0.634)

Capability = the spreadsheet agent's system prompt (`prompt.md`). Reader = azure/gpt-5.5 (strong,
less robust on long/ambiguous context → prefers explicit rules + a worked cue). Only `prompt.md`
editable. Harness re-scores; I did NOT run evaluation.

## Situation inherited
cand_0001 is champion (0.634). Iters 2–5 all REJECTED. LEDGER shows the refuted edits and the
tasks each broke. Key facts governing this iteration:
- The FRAGILE-PASSER set {267-18, 430-43, 58484, 347-49, 47699, 61-4, CF_*} flips whenever a
  broad DECISION/PERMISSION rule is added (read-scope, type-coercion, #N/A, deletion-fill,
  write-value-on-format, casing-coercion). Every rejected iter disturbed some of them.
- cand_0005 was a NO-OP yet still flipped {267-18, 430-43, 58484} + {139-16, 35747}: those tasks
  are SCORING-NOISE-sensitive. Reliable gains must come from DETERMINISTIC 0/3 zeros, not flaky
  tasks — and net gain must clear a significance/noise margin (cand_0002 netted +3 tasks yet was
  rejected at +0.007).
- Therefore: do NOT re-touch any refuted lever; add at most a NARROW, conditionally-scoped rule
  whose activation condition is FALSE on every fragile passer (guaranteeing no-op there).

## Ranked issue list (this iteration's ./trajectories/)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | change class | decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Ignored the sheet's own worked example / reference** | 39946, 10281, 14207 (all 0/3; also touches 413-15, 146-49 which supply an "attached example file") | the sheet DEMONSTRATES the exact op (reference formula, filled example, highlighted rows) but the agent substitutes an equivalent-LOOKING but wrong method | add-missing-knowledge (conditional, additive) | **SHIPPED** |
| — | Text-typed numbers dropped on read | 35747, 32975, 50526 | read-side coercion | = refuted cand_0002 type-coercion | SKIP |
| — | Write-type / "" vs blank | 585-41, 53062 | output typing | = refuted cand_0002 write-numeric | SKIP |
| — | VLOOKUP no-match representation | 31420 | #N/A vs "" | = refuted cand_0004 #N/A (threatens 53023) | SKIP |
| — | Delete-N-rows-before-marker | 269-44 | row-deletion fill | = refuted deletion-fill territory | SKIP |
| — | Per-task logic errors | 398-14 (RET−SALE sign), 6698, 4225, 48983, 53305, 53449, 55258, 157-4*, 254-34*, 34-5, 577-40 … | each a distinct wrong computation / ambiguous "current date" / env fault | not prose-fixable without hardcoding an answer | SKIP |

(*157-4/254-34 are already covered by cand_0001's macro-as-value rule; residual failures are
per-task logic, not prose-fixable.)

## Change made this iteration (ONE edit — surgical, additive, conditionally scoped)
| cluster | lever | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | add-missing-knowledge (SKILL #4/#5) + checklist clause | New bullet (prompt.md line 10): when the worksheet ITSELF demonstrates the intended result (reference formulas in neighbouring cells, a worked example row/column, or cells the instruction calls an example), treat it as the exact spec — reproduce its precise arithmetic (denominator/constant, inclusive/exclusive boundaries, rounding) and its exact output text/casing, reading those defining cells AT RUN TIME (so it still adapts to hidden files 2&3). Plus a 4th pre-finish checklist clause restating it. | Yes — see blast radius. |

### Why this is a KNOWLEDGE fix, not mere emphasis
cand_0001 line 9 tells the agent "don't hardcode a number/constant you read from the sample."
On tasks like 39946 that pushes gpt-5.5 to AVOID the very constant a reference formula legitimately
defines (`/365`), so it invents its own denominator. The new bullet resolves that tension
explicitly: reading a constant that the sheet's OWN reference formula defines is reading the spec,
not hardcoding — and doing it at run time keeps it general. That is a genuine knowledge gap the
prompt previously created, not a rule the agent knowingly violates.

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes on those exact inputs)
- **39946** (0/3): author reference formulas show `=$G$8/365*N4`; final code divided by
  `total_billed_days` instead → wrong per-day amount on all 3 files. New rule → agent reads the
  reference formula's denominator (365) at run time and reproduces it → matches.
- **10281** (0/3): reference cell I15 = `=IF(...,"PASS","FAIL")`; final output drifted on the
  result text/casing. New rule ("write PASS/FAIL exactly as shown") → exact-string match.
- **14207** (0/3): red-highlighted example rows demonstrate which rows match; code used an
  untethered substring heuristic. New rule → agent grounds the match rule in the demonstrated
  example rather than guessing.

## Blast-radius / SAFE argument
- The rule's activation condition is "the worksheet already demonstrates the intended result
  (reference formula / worked example / example cells)." On every FRAGILE passer this condition is
  FALSE: 267-18 (URL edit), 430-43 (filter), 58484 (count), 347-49 (delete), 47699 (sum), 61-4
  (merge), CF_* (conditional formatting) contain no reference formula the agent currently ignores
  → the bullet is a strict no-op there.
- Passing tasks that DO contain a reference example already produce correct output → the rule only
  reinforces behaviour they already exhibit; it never asks them to change a correct answer.
- Additive only. Loosens nothing. Touches no range/typing/deletion/formatting/error rule. The
  illustrative "/365" and "PASS/FAIL" are GENERIC worked cues for the reader, not task-specific
  answers hardcoded into agent output (no id/value/date baked in).
- Does NOT re-introduce any LEDGER-documented regressing edit (verified against iters 2–5 diffs).

## Process & features used
- 4 read-only diagnosis subagents partitioned the deterministic 0/3 zeros (sheet-level;
  cell-level A & B; flaky set). Group A surfaced the reference-example cluster with quoted
  in-sheet evidence (`=$G$8/365*N4`, `I15=IF(...,"PASS","FAIL")`, highlighted example rows).
- Read adapter replay mechanic + grader transform (established in cand_0001) to confirm reading
  reference cells at run time still generalizes across the 3 hidden inputs.
- Cross-read LEDGER + prior_iterations/*/diff.patch to exclude every refuted lever.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- All type-coercion / write-type / #N/A / deletion-fill clusters: overlap LEDGER-refuted edits
  that broke fragile passers. Not worth the regression risk on a plateaued prompt.
- ~15 per-task logic errors and the ambiguous "current date" tasks: no general prose rule fixes
  them without hardcoding a specific answer (overfitting).
- Noise-sensitive flaky tasks (139-16, 35747, …): cannot be reliably fixed by prose; flips are
  scoring noise, not prompt defects.

## Good things to PRESERVE (future iterations must not undo)
- cand_0001's four grounded rules (values-not-code, literal-not-formula, derive-dynamically,
  checklist) — all still load-bearing.
- The new reference-example rule's CONDITIONAL scoping — do not broaden it into an unconditional
  "copy nearby cells" rule (that would regress delete/replace tasks whose answer_position holds
  the OLD values to be changed).
